inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: 476,847,802 ordinary shares on issue at 17 Aug 2026 (FY2026 AR shareholder information, i.e. AFTER the August 2026 entitlement offer; 420,928,435 at 30 June) plus all 41,762,307 employee performance rights (33.1m unvested, counted in full). Held flat: future SBC is expensed in the flows, and future funding raises are charged as negative FCF (equivalent to issuing at intrinsic value) rather than as share growth -- charging both would double-count.
inputs.net_cash_note: PRO FORMA. Cash A$11.015m at 30 June 2026 plus A$30.0m net proceeds of the renounceable entitlement offer completed 11 Aug 2026 (FY2026 AR note 21). Debt A$0.363m is the remaining lease liability. Not adjusted for burn since 30 June (inside the year-1 flow), the A$0.5m Radiopharm option fee (July 2026) or the A$3.5m R&D tax incentive received Oct 2026 (both inside year-1 revenue/EBITDA). The up-to-A$5.0m Petalion commitment (Oct 2026) is inside the projected cost base, not deducted here.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 AR statement of changes in equity, employee performance rights plan expense A$2,243k (Metrics.csv StockBasedComp). No cash taxes on equity awards: rights convert by new share issue. Note the cash-flow reconciliation line 'Share-based payments 561' is a different, smaller figure; the equity-statement expense is the one used.
inputs.wacc_rationale: AUD cost of equity, no debt: ~4.4% AU 10-year bond + ~1.1 beta x 6% ERP = 11%. Same rate in all three scenarios. Clinical, partnering and funding risk is carried in the scenario flows and the 45/40/15 weights (an rNPV-style treatment), so no extra biotech premium is stacked on the rate -- risk is charged once.
inputs.lease_treatment: (A) leases as debt: the A$0.36m remaining lease liability is in net debt and no lease charge is deducted from the flows. Immaterial either way; the premises lease expires in FY27 and its renewal cost sits inside the projected cost base/D&A.
inputs.nci_treatment: None at the balance date. Petalion Therapeutics moved from a 22.5% associate to a 66% subsidiary in Oct 2026 (Medicxi holds the rest); it is a pre-clinical cost centre, its spend is in the projected burn at 100% and no NCI value is deducted. Revisit if Petalion is financed or monetised separately.
inputs.notes: MODEL CHOICE: owner-FCF component DCF (Drivers route), used as a risk-weighted scenario model. The dcf-methods routing table has no pre-profit biotech row; SPL is an operating company (not a bank, REIT, LIC, shell or deal situation), so the owner-FCF engine applies, but NOT in its usual form: there is no historical FCF or margin to extrapolate (11 straight years of negative FCF; FY2026 revenue of A$12.05m includes a one-off A$8.34m Genentech upfront, underlying ~A$3.7m). The three scenarios are therefore discrete outcomes for the DEP platform (fails to convert / one mid-sized deal / radiopharma success), built in dollars and expressed as percent-of-revenue paths, which is why early-year margins read as -170% to -370%. Probability weights do the work clinical success probabilities do in an rNPV. Historical CAGRs are not used to set growth. CAVEATS: (1) The value is dominated by the 15%-weighted bull case; treat the weighted IV as an expected value of a skewed distribution, not a point estimate. (2) No revenue, cost or milestone guidance exists; only 'runway into FY28', which calibrates year 1-2 burn at ~A$18m. (3) Deal economics (Genentech up to US$564m, Radiopharm up to A$91m) are headline maxima with undisclosed milestone schedules and royalty rates. (4) UNEXPLAINED PRICE MOVE: the stock fell ~38% in the week of 19 Oct 2026 (0.75 -> 0.465 on 2-3x normal volume) and has drifted lower since. Nothing in the filings on hand (latest: FY2026 AR, Aug 2026) explains it; the Petalion stake increase was announced the same month. The ASX announcements for Oct-Nov 2026 must be read before acting on this valuation -- if the cause was a HER2-Lu delay or a partner termination the scenario weights here are too generous. (5) R&D costs are stated net of the refundable R&D tax incentive (A$3.5m); refundability is lost above A$20m turnover, which the bull path crosses in FY29. Buybacks: none ever; the flat count is a modelling convention, and the company is a serial issuer (the Aug 2026 raise added 13% to the count at roughly A$0.57/share).

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: none -- not meaningful; scenarios are built bottom-up in dollars
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (-26%/yr: losses outrunning raises) diverges from revenue CAGR (+46-60%, which is one Genentech upfront on a tiny base) by far more than 30pp. EPS and owner FCF were negative at both ends of every window so no CAGR exists. Owner FCF (reported FCF - SBC - interest income): FY2021 -19.1, FY2022 -16.5, FY2023 -17.5, FY2024 -10.0, FY2025 -8.6, FY2026 -6.4 (A$m).
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF is 1.8x worse than reported FCF in FY2026 (-6.4 vs -3.5) because SBC (2.2) and interest on the cash pile (0.6) are both stripped.

base.narrative: Muddle-through with one real deal. FY27-28 carry no large upfront (revenue A$6-8m: products, Radiopharm option fee/exercise, research fees) while the HER2-Lu Phase 1 and consolidated Petalion spend run burn at A$18m/yr, consistent with management's 'runway into FY28'. Adequate Phase 1 data supports a mid-sized out-licence around FY29 (revenue A$15m), after which the partner carries most development cost; Genentech/Radiopharm development milestones dribble in and first royalties arrive late in the decade. Revenue reaches A$48m by year 10 with owner EBITDA of A$19m; break-even is year 7. Cumulative burn before break-even (~A$66m) exceeds current cash, i.e. at least one further raise is implied -- it is charged through the negative flows rather than through a rising share count.

bull.narrative: DEP HER2-Lu shows clearly differentiated tumour uptake/kidney sparing in humans and is licensed to a radioligand major around FY29 for a large upfront (revenue A$70m that year), in a sector where Novartis/AAA, BMS/RayzeBio and Lilly/POINT have paid up for assets. That data re-rates the whole DEP radiopharma platform: the Radiopharm option is exercised, Genentech programs advance through clinical milestones (part of the up-to-US$564m), Star Navigator converts further licences, and milestone plus royalty income compounds to A$200m by year 10 at ~78% owner-EBITDA margin (a licensor's cost base barely scales). The A$128m of unrecognised tax losses shelters profit until year 7, then cash tax ramps to 30%.

bear.narrative: The platform does not convert. DEP HER2-Lu Phase 1 dosimetry/safety is unremarkable and finds no partner, Genentech and Radiopharm programs stall pre-clinically (as DEP SN38 and DEP cabazitaxel out-licensing has for years), and no further upfronts arrive. Revenue falls back to the ~A$4.5m of product sales, royalties and research fees and grows slowly. The A$41m pro-forma cash funds two years of trial-level burn (owner EBITDA -18, -14), after which the board cuts R&D to a consumer-health/royalty shell that roughly breaks even (owner EBITDA +1.0m on A$8.5m revenue by year 10). Value is what cash is left after the wind-down plus a small residual business.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Not the 15/50/35 house default. Bear 45%: every DEP asset is pre-clinical or Phase 1, industry likelihood of approval from Phase 1 oncology is ~5%, and 20 years of platform work have produced no approved proprietary drug while SN38/cabazitaxel partnering has repeatedly slipped. Base 40%: the Genentech and Radiopharm agreements are real external validation and make one further mid-sized deal the single most likely positive outcome. Bull 15%: needs positive human data AND a large licence AND partner programs advancing -- several independent things going right -- but is well above a single-asset LOA because the platform has several shots (HER2-Lu, Genentech, Radiopharm, Petalion) and radioligand assets are being licensed/acquired on early data.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Starpharma is an option on the DEP dendrimer platform plus a cash pile that the option consumes. On a fully diluted 518.6m shares, pro-forma net cash is ~A$0.08/share against a price several times that; the market is paying roughly A$180m for the platform. The scenario build says that is only justified in the success case: muddle-through is worth about what the cash is worth today, and failure is worth close to nothing after the wind-down burn. This is a distribution, not a compounder -- size accordingly.
key_risks_to_valuation: Bull-case dependence: ~80% of weighted value comes from a 15%-probability scenario; moving that weight by 5pp moves the weighted IV by roughly a quarter.
Unexplained ~38% share price fall in the week of 19 Oct 2026 -- cause not in the filings on hand; read the ASX announcements first.

Funding: base-case cumulative burn to break-even (~A$66m) exceeds the A$41m pro-forma cash; a further raise at a depressed price would dilute more than the model's fair-value-issuance convention assumes.
DEP HER2-Lu first-in-human readout (study start guided H2 CY2026) is the swing event between the scenarios.
Milestone schedules and royalty rates for Genentech and Radiopharm are undisclosed; scenario revenue is judgment, not contract arithmetic.
Bear and near-bear paths end with terminal FCF near zero; a lower floor (continued burn funded by serial raises, as in FY2015-FY2025) would take equity value to nil.
